name: argument_arrangements
description: Named macro-arrangements for nonfiction and argument — classical oration and its progymnasmatic kin, legal, scientific, business, persuasive, dialectical, mathematical, journalistic, essayistic and homiletic forms. Many carry 'beats': [{name, position 0-1, purpose}].

classical_oration.name: classical oration
classical_oration.definition: The full six-part Ciceronian arrangement: open, narrate the facts, divide the issues, prove, refute, and close.

beats.name: exordium
beats.purpose: Win attention and goodwill; establish the speaker's standing to speak.

beats.name: narratio
beats.purpose: Lay out the facts of the case in the order most favourable to the argument.

beats.name: partitio
beats.purpose: State what is agreed, what is at issue, and in what order it will be taken.

beats.name: confirmatio
beats.purpose: Present the positive proofs, strongest arguments bracketing the weaker ones.

beats.name: refutatio
beats.purpose: Answer the strongest opposing arguments before the audience raises them.

beats.name: peroratio
beats.purpose: Recapitulate, amplify, and move the audience to act.

classical_oration.register: formal argument of any length; the ancestor of most nonfiction structure
classical_oration.caution: Six parts in six thousand words is a speech; in a book, each part is a chapter, and partitio has to be re-stated.

classical_oration.name: four-part oration
classical_oration.definition: The reduced arrangement — opening, statement of facts, proof, and close — for occasions with no contested division of issues.

beats.name: exordium
beats.purpose: Secure attention and frame the occasion.

beats.name: narratio
beats.purpose: Supply the facts the proof will depend on.

beats.name: confirmatio
beats.purpose: Prove the case, absorbing refutation into the positive line.

beats.name: peroratio
beats.purpose: Summarize and close with amplification.

classical_oration.register: op-eds, short talks, memos with an argumentative edge

classical_oration.name: prothesis and pistis
classical_oration.definition: Aristotle's minimum: state the thing, then prove it — everything else is optional.

beats.name: prothesis
beats.purpose: State the proposition to be proved, without ornament.

beats.name: pistis
beats.purpose: Supply the proofs, artistic and inartistic, that establish it.

classical_oration.effect: The useful corrective when an arrangement has grown ceremonial: cut to statement and proof and see what is missing.

classical_oration.name: insinuatio
classical_oration.definition: An indirect opening used when the audience is hostile or the case is discreditable: approach obliquely before naming the claim.
classical_oration.effect: Buys a hearing that a direct exordium would forfeit.
classical_oration.caution: If the audience notices the manoeuvre before the claim arrives, the concealment itself becomes the charge.

classical_oration.name: chreia elaboration
classical_oration.definition: The progymnasmatic eight-part expansion of a saying or anecdote into a full argument.

beats.name: praise of the author
beats.purpose: Establish the authority of the person quoted.

beats.name: paraphrase
beats.purpose: Restate the saying in the writer's own words.

beats.name: cause
beats.purpose: Explain why the saying is true.

beats.name: contrary
beats.purpose: Show what follows if the opposite were the case.

beats.name: comparison
beats.purpose: Set the case beside an analogous one.

beats.name: example
beats.purpose: Give a historical or observed instance.

beats.name: testimony
beats.purpose: Cite an authority who agrees.

beats.name: epilogue
beats.purpose: Exhort the reader to accept the saying.

classical_oration.register: training exercise; still the fastest way to turn a quotation into a 1,200-word essay

classical_oration.name: encomium
classical_oration.definition: Formal praise arranged by the standard headings of a subject's origins, upbringing, deeds and comparison.

beats.name: prologue
beats.purpose: Announce the subject and the grounds of praise.

beats.name: origin
beats.purpose: Nation, ancestry, parentage — the inherited goods.

beats.name: upbringing
beats.purpose: Education, training, habits formed.

beats.name: deeds
beats.purpose: Acts of mind, body and fortune — the substance of the praise.

beats.name: comparison
beats.purpose: Set the subject above a comparable figure.

beats.name: epilogue
beats.purpose: Close with an exhortation to emulate.

classical_oration.register: award citations, obituaries, forewords, keynote introductions

classical_oration.name: invective
classical_oration.definition: The mirror of encomium: blame arranged by the same headings, turned to censure.
classical_oration.caution: The symmetry with praise is exactly what makes it read as unfair; a single unanswered virtue costs the whole piece.

classical_oration.name: synkrisis
classical_oration.definition: Paired praise or blame in which two subjects are compared point by point on the same headings.
classical_oration.effect: The parallel headings do the arguing; a comparison that changes criteria between subjects reads instantly as rigged.

classical_oration.name: commonplace
classical_oration.definition: Amplification of a vice or virtue in general, aimed at the type rather than at a named person.
classical_oration.register: editorial, sermon, and the outrage column
classical_oration.caution: Generic denunciation persuades nobody who does not already agree; it is a heat source, not a proof.

classical_oration.name: confirmation exercise
classical_oration.definition: Establishing the credibility of a narrative by arguing that it is clear, plausible, possible, consistent and fitting.

classical_oration.name: refutation exercise
classical_oration.definition: Attacking a narrative through a fixed sequence of defects, each heading a separate line of attack.

beats.name: obscurity
beats.purpose: Show the account is unclear about who, when or how.

beats.name: implausibility
beats.purpose: Show it is unlikely on ordinary experience.

beats.name: impossibility
beats.purpose: Show it could not have happened as told.

beats.name: inconsistency
beats.purpose: Show it contradicts itself or the record.

beats.name: impropriety
beats.purpose: Show it is unbecoming of the people it describes.

beats.name: inexpediency
beats.purpose: Show that believing it would be harmful.

classical_oration.effect: A ready-made checklist for dismantling any received story; stop at the strongest two or three headings.

classical_oration.name: thesis exercise
classical_oration.definition: A general question argued without reference to particular persons or occasions, under fixed heads.

beats.name: statement of the question
beats.purpose: Pose the general question ('should one marry?').

beats.name: the lawful
beats.purpose: Argue from what is permitted or required.

beats.name: the just
beats.purpose: Argue from fairness and desert.

beats.name: the advantageous
beats.purpose: Argue from benefit and cost.

beats.name: the possible
beats.purpose: Argue from feasibility.

beats.name: the honourable
beats.purpose: Argue from what is fitting and praiseworthy.

classical_oration.name: ethopoeia
classical_oration.definition: Argument arranged as the speech a named character would plausibly deliver in a given situation.
classical_oration.effect: Converts abstract disagreement into a voice the reader has to answer.
classical_oration.register: dialogue-form nonfiction, imagined-objection passages, historical writing

classical_oration.name: deliberative arrangement
classical_oration.definition: Argument about future action organized around advantage and harm, ending in a recommendation.

beats.name: statement of the decision
beats.purpose: Name the choice actually before the audience.

beats.name: the present situation
beats.purpose: Establish the facts that constrain the choice.

beats.name: advantages of the course urged
beats.purpose: Argue expediency, security and honour.

beats.name: disadvantages of the alternatives
beats.purpose: Cost the rejected options honestly.

beats.name: call to decide
beats.purpose: Ask for the specific action, from the people who can take it.

classical_oration.register: policy writing, board papers, strategy memos

classical_oration.name: forensic arrangement
classical_oration.definition: Argument about past acts organized around accusation and defence, with justice as the governing question.
classical_oration.register: legal argument, investigative writing, accountability journalism

classical_oration.name: epideictic arrangement
classical_oration.definition: Argument of praise or blame organized around shared values on a ceremonial occasion.
classical_oration.effect: Its real work is consolidating what an audience already holds, which is why it precedes deliberation more often than it follows it.

classical_oration.name: stasis-driven arrangement
classical_oration.definition: Locate the point at which the parties actually disagree — fact, definition, quality or jurisdiction — and arrange the whole piece to that question.

beats.name: stasis of fact
beats.purpose: Did it happen? Settle or concede before moving on.

beats.name: stasis of definition
beats.purpose: What shall we call it? Name the act correctly.

beats.name: stasis of quality
beats.purpose: How serious, how justified, how mitigated?

beats.name: stasis of jurisdiction
beats.purpose: Is this the right forum and the right procedure?

classical_oration.effect: The single highest-leverage diagnostic in argument: most stalled disputes are two parties arguing at different stases.

legal_forms.name: irac
legal_forms.definition: Issue, rule, application, conclusion — the baseline unit of legal analysis.

beats.name: issue
beats.purpose: State the legal question in dispute.

beats.name: rule
beats.purpose: State the governing law with authority.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Apply the rule to these facts, both ways where reasonable.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Answer the question asked.

legal_forms.caution: Taught as a container and used as one; the analysis lives in application, which is where student writing is thinnest.

legal_forms.name: creac
legal_forms.definition: Conclusion, rule, explanation, application, conclusion — IRAC with the answer first and a separate rule-explanation section.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Give the answer immediately, as a thesis.

beats.name: rule
beats.purpose: State the governing standard.

beats.name: explanation
beats.purpose: Illustrate how courts have applied the rule in analogous cases.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Map those cases onto the present facts.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Restate the answer, now earned.

legal_forms.name: crac
legal_forms.definition: Conclusion, rule, application, conclusion — the compressed thesis-first variant for readers who know the law.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: State the outcome as a claim.

beats.name: rule
beats.purpose: Supply the authority in one or two sentences.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Argue the facts under the rule.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Close on the requested relief.

legal_forms.register: briefs and memoranda for expert readers

legal_forms.name: treat
legal_forms.definition: Thesis, rule, explanation, application, thesis — a persuasive framing that opens and closes on the advocated proposition.

beats.name: thesis
beats.purpose: Assert the proposition this section proves.

beats.name: rule
beats.purpose: State the legal standard, framed favourably but accurately.

beats.name: explanation
beats.purpose: Develop the rule through precedent.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Apply to the record, distinguishing adverse cases.

beats.name: thesis
beats.purpose: Restate the proposition as now established.

legal_forms.name: ilac
legal_forms.definition: Issue, law, application, conclusion — the common-law teaching variant that separates finding the law from stating a rule.

beats.name: issue
beats.purpose: Identify the question raised by the facts.

beats.name: law
beats.purpose: Set out statute and authority, including uncertainty.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Reason from law to facts.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: State the likely outcome and its confidence.

legal_forms.name: mirat
legal_forms.definition: Material facts, issue, rule, application, tentative conclusion — the variant that makes fact selection an explicit step.

beats.name: material facts
beats.purpose: Select and state only the facts that bear on the issue.

beats.name: issue
beats.purpose: Frame the legal question those facts raise.

beats.name: rule
beats.purpose: State the applicable law.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Reason both sides of the application.

beats.name: tentative conclusion
beats.purpose: Give a qualified answer, flagging what would change it.

legal_forms.effect: The 'tentative' is the point: it licenses honest uncertainty that IRAC's 'conclusion' suppresses.

legal_forms.name: case brief
legal_forms.definition: Standard reduction of a decided case to its usable parts for later argument.

beats.name: facts
beats.purpose: The operative facts the court treated as material.

beats.name: procedural posture
beats.purpose: How the case arrived and under what standard of review.

beats.name: issue
beats.purpose: The question the court answered.

beats.name: holding
beats.purpose: The answer, stated narrowly.

beats.name: reasoning
beats.purpose: The chain that got the court there.

beats.name: disposition
beats.purpose: What the court ordered.

legal_forms.name: appellate brief structure
legal_forms.definition: The conventional order of a brief on appeal, from questions presented to requested relief.

beats.name: questions presented
beats.purpose: Frame the issues in terms that suggest the answer.

beats.name: statement of the case
beats.purpose: Narrate the record persuasively but without argument.

beats.name: summary of argument
beats.purpose: Give the whole argument in a page, for the judge who reads no further.

beats.name: argument
beats.purpose: Develop each point under its own heading, strongest first.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: State the precise relief sought.

legal_forms.caution: The summary is the most-read section and the most commonly written last and worst.

legal_forms.name: question presented
legal_forms.definition: A single-sentence issue statement built as under-does-when: governing law, legal question, key facts.
legal_forms.example: Under the FLSA, does a courier qualify as an employee when the platform sets prices, routes and penalties?
legal_forms.effect: Loads the facts that decide the case into the question itself.

legal_forms.name: persuasive statement of facts
legal_forms.definition: A fact section that argues by selection, order and emphasis while remaining scrupulously accurate.
legal_forms.caution: One overstated fact costs the credibility of every other; the adversary reads this section hunting.

legal_forms.name: point heading hierarchy
legal_forms.definition: Argument headings written as complete propositions so that the table of contents reads as the outline of the argument.
legal_forms.effect: A brief whose contents page states the case in six sentences has already made half its argument.

legal_forms.name: analogical precedent reasoning
legal_forms.definition: Derive a rule from decided cases, compare their material facts to the present ones, and argue that like cases must be decided alike.

beats.name: rule from precedent
beats.purpose: State the principle the prior cases share.

beats.name: factual comparison
beats.purpose: Line up the material facts side by side.

beats.name: conclusion of likeness
beats.purpose: Argue the present case falls on the established side of the line.

legal_forms.name: distinguishing precedent
legal_forms.definition: Accept the adverse case and argue that a material difference makes its rule inapplicable here.
legal_forms.caution: The difference must be material to the reason for the rule, not merely a difference the record happens to contain.

legal_forms.name: burden-shifting framework
legal_forms.definition: A three-stage arrangement in which each party in turn carries a defined burden of production.

beats.name: prima facie case
beats.purpose: Claimant establishes the minimum elements.

beats.name: legitimate justification
beats.purpose: Respondent articulates a lawful reason.

beats.name: pretext
beats.purpose: Claimant shows the stated reason is not the real one.

legal_forms.register: employment and discrimination argument; a useful general template wherever a rebuttable presumption exists

legal_forms.name: element-by-element analysis
legal_forms.definition: Arrange the argument by the elements of the claim, disposing of each in order and conceding the ones not in dispute.
legal_forms.effect: Conceding uncontested elements early buys credibility for the contested one.

legal_forms.name: syllogistic legal proof
legal_forms.definition: State the rule as the major premise, the facts as the minor, and the outcome as the conclusion.
legal_forms.caution: Almost every real dispute is about the minor premise; a brief that only polishes the syllogism has not argued the case.

legal_forms.name: policy argument
legal_forms.definition: Argue from the consequences of a rule — institutional competence, administrability, incentives — rather than from its sources.
legal_forms.register: appellate advocacy, regulatory comment, law review
legal_forms.caution: Weakest where the text is clearest; a policy lead against plain language signals that the text is against you.

legal_forms.name: bobbitt's modalities
legal_forms.definition: The six recognized forms of constitutional argument — textual, historical, structural, doctrinal, ethical, prudential — used as an arrangement checklist.
legal_forms.effect: Running a claim through all six exposes which modality your case actually rests on, and which the other side will use.

legal_forms.name: oral argument roadmap
legal_forms.definition: An opening that states the relief sought and the two or three points to be made, so the bench knows where interruptions fit.
legal_forms.caution: More than three points and the roadmap becomes a list the court will not hold.

scientific_forms.name: imrad
scientific_forms.definition: Introduction, methods, results and discussion — the standard arrangement of the empirical research article.

beats.name: introduction
beats.purpose: Establish the problem and the gap this study fills.

beats.name: methods
beats.purpose: Describe procedure in enough detail to be repeated.

beats.name: results
beats.purpose: Report findings without interpretation.

beats.name: discussion
beats.purpose: Interpret, bound, and connect back to the gap.

scientific_forms.caution: The order of writing is rarely the order of reading; most readers go abstract, figures, discussion, methods.

scientific_forms.name: hourglass model
scientific_forms.definition: Broad framing narrowing to a specific study, then widening again to implications.

beats.name: broad context
beats.purpose: Why this domain matters to a non-specialist.

beats.name: narrowing
beats.purpose: Move from field to question to hypothesis.

beats.name: the neck
beats.purpose: The specific study: methods and results at maximum precision.

beats.name: widening
beats.purpose: What the result means for the question.

beats.name: broad implications
beats.purpose: What it means for the field.

scientific_forms.effect: Gives readers a symmetric entrance and exit, which is why abstracts written to this shape summarize cleanly.

scientific_forms.name: cars model
scientific_forms.definition: Swales's three rhetorical moves for research introductions: establish a territory, establish a niche, occupy the niche.

beats.name: establishing a territory
beats.purpose: Claim centrality, generalize the topic, review prior work.

beats.name: establishing a niche
beats.purpose: Counter-claim, indicate a gap, raise a question or continue a tradition.

beats.name: occupying the niche
beats.purpose: State the present work's purpose, announce findings, preview structure.

scientific_forms.effect: Makes the gap explicit, which is the move most rejected introductions omit.

scientific_forms.name: ocar
scientific_forms.definition: Opening, challenge, action, resolution — Schimel's story-shaped arrangement for a scientific paper.

beats.name: opening
beats.purpose: Establish the setting and the characters of the problem.

beats.name: challenge
beats.purpose: State the unresolved question that creates tension.

beats.name: action
beats.purpose: What was done and what was found.

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: How the finding answers the challenge.

scientific_forms.register: papers, proposals and talks aimed beyond the immediate subfield

scientific_forms.name: ldr
scientific_forms.definition: Lead, development, resolution — the front-loaded variant that states the conclusion first and develops it afterwards.

beats.name: lead
beats.purpose: State the central finding immediately.

beats.name: development
beats.purpose: Supply the evidence and reasoning behind it.

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: Close on significance rather than suspense.

scientific_forms.register: abstracts, executive-facing science writing, press releases

scientific_forms.name: structured abstract
scientific_forms.definition: A fixed-heading abstract that forces each element of the study to be stated separately.

beats.name: background
beats.purpose: Why the question matters.

beats.name: objective
beats.purpose: The specific aim, in one sentence.

beats.name: methods
beats.purpose: Design, setting, participants, measures.

beats.name: results
beats.purpose: Primary outcome with effect size and interval.

beats.name: conclusions
beats.purpose: What follows, bounded by the design.

scientific_forms.caution: The headings make omissions conspicuous, which is their purpose and the reason authors resist them.

scientific_forms.name: prisma review structure
scientific_forms.definition: The reporting arrangement for systematic reviews: protocol, search, screening, extraction, synthesis, risk of bias.

beats.name: protocol and registration
beats.purpose: Declare the question and method before looking.

beats.name: search strategy
beats.purpose: State sources, terms, and dates so the search is reproducible.

beats.name: screening and eligibility
beats.purpose: Account for every record, included and excluded.

beats.name: data extraction
beats.purpose: State what was pulled from each study and by whom.

beats.name: synthesis
beats.purpose: Combine results, quantitatively or narratively.

beats.name: risk of bias
beats.purpose: Assess study quality and its effect on the conclusion.

scientific_forms.name: registered report
scientific_forms.definition: A two-stage arrangement in which rationale and method are reviewed and accepted before data are collected.

beats.name: stage 1: rationale and method
beats.purpose: Question, hypotheses, design, analysis plan, power.

beats.name: in-principle acceptance
beats.purpose: Editorial commitment independent of outcome.

beats.name: stage 2: results and discussion
beats.purpose: Report as planned, separating pre-registered from exploratory analysis.

scientific_forms.effect: Structurally removes the incentive to arrange a paper around whichever result happened to be significant.

scientific_forms.name: specific aims page
scientific_forms.definition: The one-page grant arrangement: significance, gap, long-term goal, objective, aims, and expected impact.

beats.name: the hook
beats.purpose: Name the problem in terms the panel already cares about.

beats.name: the gap
beats.purpose: State what is not known and why the gap blocks progress.

beats.name: objective and hypothesis
beats.purpose: Say precisely what this project will do and expect.

beats.name: the aims
beats.purpose: Two or three non-dependent aims, each testable.

beats.name: payoff
beats.purpose: State the expected impact if the aims succeed.

scientific_forms.caution: Aims that depend on one another turn one failed experiment into a failed project; reviewers look for this first.

scientific_forms.name: case report
scientific_forms.definition: Clinical narrative arrangement: presentation, history, investigations, management, outcome, discussion.

beats.name: presentation
beats.purpose: Who presented, with what, when.

beats.name: history and examination
beats.purpose: Relevant background and findings.

beats.name: investigations
beats.purpose: Tests performed and results.

beats.name: management
beats.purpose: Intervention and its rationale.

beats.name: outcome and follow-up
beats.purpose: What happened and over what period.

beats.name: discussion
beats.purpose: Why this case is instructive.

scientific_forms.name: soap note
scientific_forms.definition: Subjective, objective, assessment, plan — the clinical note arrangement that separates report from observation from judgement from action.

beats.name: subjective
beats.purpose: What the patient reports, in their terms.

beats.name: objective
beats.purpose: Measured and observed findings.

beats.name: assessment
beats.purpose: The clinician's interpretation and differential.

beats.name: plan
beats.purpose: What will be done and when it will be reviewed.

scientific_forms.effect: Generalizes well beyond medicine as a discipline for keeping observation and inference in separate paragraphs.

scientific_forms.name: literature review funnel
scientific_forms.definition: Survey arranged from the broadest relevant literature down to the specific studies the present work engages.
scientific_forms.caution: A funnel with no exit is a bibliography; the narrow end must land on a claim about what the field has not settled.

scientific_forms.name: conference abstract
scientific_forms.definition: A compressed self-contained arrangement — question, method, result, significance — written to be selected rather than read.
scientific_forms.caution: Written before the data exist more often than anyone admits; keep the claim inside what the design can produce.

business_forms.name: scqa
business_forms.definition: Situation, complication, question, answer — Minto's opening arrangement, which manufactures a question the reader wants answered.

beats.name: situation
beats.purpose: State the stable, uncontested background.

beats.name: complication
beats.purpose: Introduce the change or problem that disturbs it.

beats.name: question
beats.purpose: Name the question the complication raises.

beats.name: answer
beats.purpose: Give the answer, which becomes the document's governing thought.

business_forms.effect: The reader arrives at the thesis already wanting it, which is the whole trick.
business_forms.caution: If the situation is not genuinely uncontested, the reader argues with paragraph one and never reaches the answer.

business_forms.name: pyramid principle
business_forms.definition: Lead with the governing thought, support it with a small set of mutually exclusive key lines, and support each of those in turn.

beats.name: governing thought
beats.purpose: The single answer the whole document argues.

beats.name: key line
beats.purpose: Three to five supporting arguments, collectively sufficient.

beats.name: support
beats.purpose: Data and reasoning under each key-line argument.

beats.name: synthesis
beats.purpose: Restate the governing thought as now supported.

business_forms.register: consulting decks, executive memos, board papers

business_forms.name: mece grouping
business_forms.definition: Organize supporting arguments so that they are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.
business_forms.effect: Overlapping groups make an argument feel repetitive; incomplete ones make it feel evasive.
business_forms.caution: Strict MECE is often unattainable; say which dimension you cut on rather than pretending the cut is natural.

business_forms.name: bluf
business_forms.definition: Bottom line up front: the recommendation or finding in the first sentence, with support following.

beats.name: bottom line
beats.purpose: State the conclusion or ask in one sentence.

beats.name: so what
beats.purpose: Why it matters to this reader now.

beats.name: support
beats.purpose: The evidence, ordered by weight.

beats.name: next step
beats.purpose: The specific action and owner.

business_forms.name: decision memo
business_forms.definition: Arrangement for a document whose purpose is to obtain one decision from one group.

beats.name: the decision requested
beats.purpose: Name the choice and who must make it.

beats.name: background
beats.purpose: Only the context needed to evaluate the options.

beats.name: options
beats.purpose: Two or three real options, each costed.

beats.name: recommendation
beats.purpose: Which one, and the reasoning.

beats.name: risks and mitigations
beats.purpose: What could go wrong and what would be done.

beats.name: the ask
beats.purpose: Approval sought, by when.

business_forms.caution: Options padded to make the recommendation obvious are recognized immediately and cost trust.

business_forms.name: working backwards
business_forms.definition: Write the launch announcement and customer FAQ before building anything, and arrange the plan around them.

beats.name: press release
beats.purpose: Describe the finished product to the customer in their language.

beats.name: customer faq
beats.purpose: Answer what a sceptical customer would ask.

beats.name: internal faq
beats.purpose: Answer what a sceptical colleague would ask about feasibility and cost.

business_forms.effect: Forces the value proposition to survive being stated plainly before resources are committed.

business_forms.name: narrative memo
business_forms.definition: A prose document read silently at the start of a meeting, replacing slides with complete sentences and full arguments.
business_forms.effect: Prose cannot hide a missing argument the way a bullet can; the discipline is in the paragraphs, not the page count.

business_forms.name: pitch deck arc
business_forms.definition: The conventional investor sequence from problem through solution, market, model, traction, team and ask.

beats.name: problem
beats.purpose: Whose pain, how expensive, how frequent.

beats.name: solution
beats.purpose: What you built and why it addresses that pain.

beats.name: market
beats.purpose: Size and reachability of the buying population.

beats.name: business model
beats.purpose: How money is made and kept.

beats.name: traction
beats.purpose: Evidence that this is already working.

beats.name: team
beats.purpose: Why these people win this specific race.

beats.name: the ask
beats.purpose: Amount, use of funds, milestone it buys.

business_forms.name: business case structure
business_forms.definition: Problem, options, costs and benefits, risks, and recommendation, arranged to support an investment decision.

business_forms.name: star method
business_forms.definition: Situation, task, action, result — the standard arrangement for narrating one's own contribution.

beats.name: situation
beats.purpose: Set the context briefly and concretely.

beats.name: task
beats.purpose: State what you specifically were responsible for.

beats.name: action
beats.purpose: What you did, in the first person singular.

beats.name: result
beats.purpose: Quantified outcome and what you learned.

business_forms.caution: The action beat is where 'we' creeps in and erases the claim.

business_forms.name: sbi feedback
business_forms.definition: Situation, behaviour, impact — feedback arranged so that observation precedes interpretation.

beats.name: situation
beats.purpose: When and where, specifically.

beats.name: behaviour
beats.purpose: What was observable, stated without adjectives of character.

beats.name: impact
beats.purpose: The effect on you, the team, or the work.

business_forms.effect: Keeps feedback arguable on facts rather than on the recipient's personality.

business_forms.name: spin sequence
business_forms.definition: Situation, problem, implication, need-payoff — a questioning order that lets the buyer state the value.

beats.name: situation questions
beats.purpose: Establish facts about the buyer's context.

beats.name: problem questions
beats.purpose: Surface difficulties and dissatisfactions.

beats.name: implication questions
beats.purpose: Make the cost of the problem explicit.

beats.name: need-payoff questions
beats.purpose: Have the buyer articulate the value of solving it.

business_forms.register: consultative selling; also useful for internal advocacy

business_forms.name: elevator pitch
business_forms.definition: A thirty-second arrangement — who, what problem, why you, what you want — designed for a single unrepeatable encounter.
business_forms.caution: Compression is not the difficulty; deciding what to omit is.

persuasion_sequences.name: monroe's motivated sequence
persuasion_sequences.definition: A five-step persuasive order that ends by asking for a specific act.

beats.name: attention
beats.purpose: Arrest the audience with a fact, story or question.

beats.name: need
beats.purpose: Establish a problem that touches them directly.

beats.name: satisfaction
beats.purpose: Present a solution that meets the stated need.

beats.name: visualization
beats.purpose: Show the future with the solution adopted and without it.

beats.name: action
beats.purpose: Ask for one concrete, immediate step.

persuasion_sequences.caution: The visualization step is where the sequence turns manipulative if the futures are not honestly drawn.

persuasion_sequences.name: aida
persuasion_sequences.definition: Attention, interest, desire, action — the oldest copywriting funnel.

beats.name: attention
beats.purpose: Stop the reader.

beats.name: interest
beats.purpose: Make the subject relevant to them.

beats.name: desire
beats.purpose: Convert relevance into wanting.

beats.name: action
beats.purpose: Remove friction from the next step.

persuasion_sequences.name: problem-agitate-solve
persuasion_sequences.definition: Name the reader's problem, intensify their sense of its cost, then offer the resolution.

beats.name: problem
beats.purpose: Name the pain in the reader's own words.

beats.name: agitate
beats.purpose: Make the consequences of inaction vivid and near.

beats.name: solve
beats.purpose: Present the remedy and the first step.

persuasion_sequences.caution: The agitation step is the most abused move in commercial prose; the honest version agitates only with true consequences.

persuasion_sequences.name: before-after-bridge
persuasion_sequences.definition: Show the current unsatisfactory state, the improved state, and the bridge that connects them.

beats.name: before
beats.purpose: Describe the reader's world as it is.

beats.name: after
beats.purpose: Describe it as it could be, concretely.

beats.name: bridge
beats.purpose: Name what gets them from one to the other.

persuasion_sequences.name: four ps
persuasion_sequences.definition: Promise, picture, proof, push — a persuasive order that pairs every claim with evidence before asking.

beats.name: promise
beats.purpose: State the benefit as a claim.

beats.name: picture
beats.purpose: Make the benefit imaginable in specifics.

beats.name: proof
beats.purpose: Supply evidence that the promise is kept.

beats.name: push
beats.purpose: Ask for the action while the proof is fresh.

persuasion_sequences.name: features-advantages-benefits
persuasion_sequences.definition: Move from what a thing is, to what it does, to what that means for this audience.

beats.name: feature
beats.purpose: State the attribute factually.

beats.name: advantage
beats.purpose: State what the attribute makes possible.

beats.name: benefit
beats.purpose: State what that is worth to this specific reader.

persuasion_sequences.caution: Most technical writing stops at the feature; most marketing skips to the benefit and cannot support it.

persuasion_sequences.name: foot-in-the-door
persuasion_sequences.definition: Secure agreement to a small request first, so that the larger request is consistent with a commitment already made.
persuasion_sequences.caution: An influence technique before it is an arrangement; disclosing that a sequence is running usually defuses it.

persuasion_sequences.name: door-in-the-face
persuasion_sequences.definition: Open with a request expected to be refused, then retreat to the request actually wanted.
persuasion_sequences.effect: Works through reciprocal concession rather than through the merits of the second request.
persuasion_sequences.caution: One transparent use costs the relationship the technique was borrowing against.

persuasion_sequences.name: inoculation
persuasion_sequences.definition: Pre-expose the audience to a weakened form of the opposing argument together with its refutation, building resistance to the full version.

beats.name: forewarning
beats.purpose: Tell the audience an attack on this belief is coming.

beats.name: weakened attack
beats.purpose: Present the counterargument in a manageable form.

beats.name: refutational preemption
beats.purpose: Answer it, giving the audience the counter-arguments to reuse.

persuasion_sequences.effect: The best-evidenced defensive arrangement in persuasion research.

persuasion_sequences.name: two-sided refutational message
persuasion_sequences.definition: Present both sides and explicitly refute the opposing one, rather than presenting your side alone.
persuasion_sequences.effect: Outperforms one-sided messages with educated or opposed audiences, and inoculates against later counter-messaging.
persuasion_sequences.caution: Two-sided without refutation is worse than one-sided: it supplies the opposition's case for free.

persuasion_sequences.name: fear appeal with efficacy
persuasion_sequences.definition: Establish threat severity and personal susceptibility, then supply a response the audience believes is effective and within their power.

beats.name: severity
beats.purpose: Show the threat is serious.

beats.name: susceptibility
beats.purpose: Show it applies to this audience.

beats.name: response efficacy
beats.purpose: Show the recommended action works.

beats.name: self-efficacy
beats.purpose: Show the audience can actually take it.

persuasion_sequences.caution: Threat without efficacy produces defensive avoidance — the audience controls the fear instead of the danger.

dialectical_forms.name: rogerian argument
dialectical_forms.definition: An arrangement that establishes common ground and states the opposing view sympathetically before advancing one's own.

beats.name: introduction of the issue
beats.purpose: Frame the problem as shared rather than as a contest.

beats.name: the opposing position
beats.purpose: State it so its holders would accept the statement.

beats.name: contexts where it is valid
beats.purpose: Concede where the opposing view is right.

beats.name: the writer's position
beats.purpose: State one's own view without triumph.

beats.name: contexts where it is valid
beats.purpose: Bound one's own claim honestly.

beats.name: benefits of adoption
beats.purpose: Show the opponent what they gain by moving.

dialectical_forms.caution: Slow and easily read as insincere if the concessions are token; the fair statement must cost something.

dialectical_forms.name: thesis-antithesis-synthesis
dialectical_forms.definition: Advance a position, develop its strongest opposition, and resolve both into a third position that preserves what each got right.

beats.name: thesis
beats.purpose: State the position in its strongest form.

beats.name: antithesis
beats.purpose: Develop the opposition with equal force.

beats.name: synthesis
beats.purpose: Show what survives of both and on what higher terms.

dialectical_forms.caution: The synthesis must genuinely resolve the tension; splitting the difference is arithmetic, not dialectic.

dialectical_forms.name: scholastic disputatio
dialectical_forms.definition: The medieval question form: pose a question, marshal the apparent answer, cite the authority against it, resolve, and answer each objection in turn.

beats.name: quaestio
beats.purpose: Pose the question as answerable yes or no.

beats.name: videtur quod
beats.purpose: Set out the strongest objections to the answer to be given.

beats.name: sed contra
beats.purpose: Cite the authority or argument on the other side.

beats.name: respondeo
beats.purpose: Give the reasoned determination.

beats.name: ad primum
beats.purpose: Answer each objection individually, in order.

dialectical_forms.effect: The objections come first and are stated by the author, which makes evasion structurally visible.
dialectical_forms.register: philosophy, theology; a strong template for any FAQ-shaped argument

dialectical_forms.name: socratic examination
dialectical_forms.definition: Question an interlocutor's confident claim until its consequences contradict something else they hold.

beats.name: elicit the claim
beats.purpose: Get the position stated clearly and voluntarily.

beats.name: secure premises
beats.purpose: Obtain assent to propositions that seem unrelated.

beats.name: derive the contradiction
beats.purpose: Show the premises are inconsistent with the claim.

beats.name: aporia
beats.purpose: Leave the interlocutor without the belief and without a replacement.

dialectical_forms.caution: In writing, an interlocutor who exists only to be wrong reads as a straw man with dialogue tags.

dialectical_forms.name: toulmin layout
dialectical_forms.definition: The anatomy of a single argument — claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier, rebuttal — used as an arrangement for contested reasoning.

beats.name: claim
beats.purpose: The proposition to be accepted.

beats.name: grounds
beats.purpose: The data or facts it rests on.

beats.name: warrant
beats.purpose: The principle licensing the move from grounds to claim.

beats.name: backing
beats.purpose: Support for the warrant itself, where it is not obvious.

beats.name: qualifier
beats.purpose: The strength claimed: presumably, probably, necessarily.

beats.name: rebuttal
beats.purpose: The conditions under which the claim would not hold.

dialectical_forms.effect: Unstated warrants are where most nonfiction arguments actually fail; writing them out is the diagnostic.

dialectical_forms.name: dissoi logoi
dialectical_forms.definition: Set out contrasting arguments on the same question without resolving them, exhibiting the case on both sides.
dialectical_forms.register: teaching, exploratory writing, judicial opinion summarizing a split

dialectical_forms.name: in utramque partem
dialectical_forms.definition: Argue both sides of a question in turn as a method of arriving at the more defensible one.
dialectical_forms.effect: Discovery procedure as much as arrangement; the side that is harder to argue well is usually the true one.

dialectical_forms.name: steelmanning
dialectical_forms.definition: Reconstruct the opposing position in the strongest form its holders would endorse, then argue against that.
dialectical_forms.caution: A steelman the opponent does not recognize is a different argument you have just won.

dialectical_forms.name: devil's advocate
dialectical_forms.definition: Assign or adopt the contrary position deliberately so that a consensus has to be defended before it is acted on.
dialectical_forms.register: decision meetings, editorial review, red teams
dialectical_forms.caution: Known to be an assigned role, it is easily discounted; genuine dissent outperforms rehearsed dissent.

dialectical_forms.name: platonic dialogue
dialectical_forms.definition: Argument staged as conversation between differentiated characters whose positions develop under questioning.
dialectical_forms.effect: Lets a writer hold several live positions at once without adjudicating prematurely.
dialectical_forms.caution: Requires characters with independent motives; otherwise it is a monologue with quotation marks.

dialectical_forms.name: catechetical form
dialectical_forms.definition: Fixed question and answer pairs arranged so that each answer prepares the next question.
dialectical_forms.caution: Assumes the reader's questions; a catechism answering questions nobody asked is the commonest FAQ failure.

dialectical_forms.name: policy debate stock issues
dialectical_forms.definition: The affirmative burden decomposed into fixed issues that a plan must satisfy.

beats.name: topicality
beats.purpose: Show the proposal is within the question under debate.

beats.name: harms
beats.purpose: Establish significant harm in the status quo.

beats.name: inherency
beats.purpose: Show the status quo will not fix it without the change.

beats.name: solvency
beats.purpose: Show the plan actually remedies the harm.

beats.name: advantages versus disadvantages
beats.purpose: Net-benefit the plan against its costs.

dialectical_forms.effect: Inherency is the issue most policy writing skips and most opponents attack.

dialectical_forms.name: four-step refutation
dialectical_forms.definition: They say, but, because, therefore — a compact unit for answering a specific opposing argument.

beats.name: they say
beats.purpose: State the opposing claim accurately and briefly.

beats.name: but
beats.purpose: State your response as a claim.

beats.name: because
beats.purpose: Give the evidence or reasoning.

beats.name: therefore
beats.purpose: State what follows for the larger argument.

dialectical_forms.name: concession and rebuttal
dialectical_forms.definition: Grant a genuine point to the opposition and show that the main claim survives it.
dialectical_forms.effect: The cheapest credibility available in argument, provided the conceded point is one the reader believed mattered.

proof_strategies.name: direct proof
proof_strategies.definition: Derive the conclusion from the hypotheses by a chain of accepted inferences.
proof_strategies.register: mathematics; the model for any deductive argument

proof_strategies.name: proof by contradiction
proof_strategies.definition: Assume the negation of the claim and derive a contradiction, establishing the claim.
proof_strategies.caution: Often hides a direct proof; readers understand the constructive version better where one exists.

proof_strategies.name: proof by contraposition
proof_strategies.definition: Prove 'if not Q then not P' in place of 'if P then Q'.
proof_strategies.effect: Useful when the negation of the conclusion is more tractable than the hypothesis.

proof_strategies.name: mathematical induction
proof_strategies.definition: Establish a base case and an inductive step that carries the property from each case to the next.

beats.name: statement
beats.purpose: Say precisely what is being proved for all n.

beats.name: base case
beats.purpose: Verify the smallest case explicitly.

beats.name: inductive hypothesis
beats.purpose: Assume the property at n, stating it exactly.

beats.name: inductive step
beats.purpose: Derive the property at n+1 from the hypothesis.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Invoke induction to conclude for all n.

proof_strategies.caution: The base case is where published proofs most often fail, because it is the part nobody rereads.

proof_strategies.name: strong induction
proof_strategies.definition: Assume the property for all cases below n rather than only at n-1.
proof_strategies.effect: Required whenever the step needs more than its immediate predecessor, as in recursion on divisors.

proof_strategies.name: structural induction
proof_strategies.definition: Prove a property for all elements of a recursively defined structure by proving it for constructors.
proof_strategies.register: computer science, formal semantics, type theory

proof_strategies.name: proof by exhaustion
proof_strategies.definition: Partition the possibilities into finitely many cases and prove the claim in each.

beats.name: partition
beats.purpose: Show the cases are exhaustive and, ideally, disjoint.

beats.name: case analysis
beats.purpose: Prove the claim within each case.

beats.name: collection
beats.purpose: Conclude that the claim holds generally.

proof_strategies.caution: The exhaustiveness of the partition is the load-bearing step and the one most often asserted.

proof_strategies.name: constructive proof
proof_strategies.definition: Establish existence by exhibiting the object, or an algorithm that produces it.
proof_strategies.effect: Strongest form of an existence claim because it hands the reader the thing itself.

proof_strategies.name: nonconstructive proof
proof_strategies.definition: Establish that an object must exist without producing one.
proof_strategies.caution: Applied readers frequently want the object; say early which kind of proof you are giving.

proof_strategies.name: proof by counterexample
proof_strategies.definition: Refute a universal claim by exhibiting one instance where it fails.
proof_strategies.effect: The cheapest decisive move in argument, and the reason universal claims should be made carefully.

proof_strategies.name: diagonal argument
proof_strategies.definition: Construct an object that differs from every member of a supposed enumeration in at least one place.

proof_strategies.name: pigeonhole argument
proof_strategies.definition: Show that placing more objects than containers forces at least one container to hold several.
proof_strategies.effect: Yields existence results from counting alone, with no construction required.

proof_strategies.name: probabilistic method
proof_strategies.definition: Show an object with the desired property exists by proving that a random object has it with positive probability.

proof_strategies.name: infinite descent
proof_strategies.definition: Show that any solution would generate a strictly smaller one, which is impossible in the positive integers.

proof_strategies.name: existence and uniqueness proof
proof_strategies.definition: Prove separately that a solution exists and that there is at most one.

beats.name: existence
beats.purpose: Exhibit or establish at least one solution.

beats.name: uniqueness
beats.purpose: Assume two solutions and show they coincide.

beats.name: consequence
beats.purpose: State what the uniqueness licenses — usually a definition.

proof_strategies.name: bijective proof
proof_strategies.definition: Establish that two counts are equal by constructing an explicit one-to-one correspondence.
proof_strategies.effect: Explains why two quantities are equal instead of merely verifying that they are.

proof_strategies.name: double counting
proof_strategies.definition: Count the same set two ways and equate the results.
proof_strategies.register: combinatorics; also a general argumentative move for reconciling two accounts of one quantity

proof_strategies.name: lemma-theorem-corollary architecture
proof_strategies.definition: Arrange a long proof as small proved lemmas, the main theorem, and consequences drawn cheaply afterwards.

beats.name: definitions
beats.purpose: Fix the objects and notation once.

beats.name: lemmas
beats.purpose: Prove the reusable technical steps in isolation.

beats.name: theorem
beats.purpose: Assemble the lemmas into the main result.

beats.name: corollaries
beats.purpose: Draw the consequences that now cost one line each.

proof_strategies.effect: Keeps the main argument short enough to be checked; also the best available structure for long nonfiction chapters.

proof_strategies.name: proof sketch then details
proof_strategies.definition: Give the idea of the proof in a paragraph before the formal argument.
proof_strategies.effect: Lets a reader decide whether to read the details, and lets them read the details knowing where they are going.

proof_strategies.name: without loss of generality
proof_strategies.definition: Reduce the cases to be treated by arguing that symmetry or relabelling makes the remainder equivalent.
proof_strategies.caution: The most-abused phrase in mathematical writing; the reduction must be stated and justified, not merely invoked.

journalism_forms.name: inverted pyramid
journalism_forms.definition: Most newsworthy information first, supporting detail in descending order of importance.

beats.name: lede
beats.purpose: The single most important fact, in one sentence.

beats.name: supporting detail
beats.purpose: Attribution, the second-most-important facts, immediate context.

beats.name: background
beats.purpose: History and prior developments.

beats.name: residual detail
beats.purpose: Material that can be cut from the bottom without damage.

journalism_forms.effect: Designed for a reader who stops anywhere and an editor who cuts from the end.
journalism_forms.caution: Zero narrative tension by construction; it is a delivery mechanism, not a shape.

journalism_forms.name: wall street journal formula
journalism_forms.definition: Open on a specific person, widen to the trend, develop it, and return to the person at the close.

beats.name: anecdotal lede
beats.purpose: One named individual in a concrete moment.

beats.name: nut graf
beats.purpose: State the larger story the anecdote illustrates and why now.

beats.name: development
beats.purpose: Evidence, sources, counter-view, scale.

beats.name: return to the person
beats.purpose: Close on the opening subject, now differently understood.

journalism_forms.caution: The anecdote must be representative; a vivid outlier at the top misleads for the length of the piece.

journalism_forms.name: wine glass structure
journalism_forms.definition: An inverted-pyramid news top joined to a chronological narrative bottom.

beats.name: news top
beats.purpose: Deliver what happened, for readers who need only that.

beats.name: turn
beats.purpose: Signal the shift to narrative — 'It began three weeks earlier.'

beats.name: chronology
beats.purpose: Tell the story in order, from the beginning.

beats.name: close
beats.purpose: End on the moment or line that carries the meaning.

journalism_forms.name: nut graf
journalism_forms.definition: The paragraph that states what the story is about, why it matters, and why it is running now.
journalism_forms.effect: The contract with the reader; a feature without one is a set of scenes.
journalism_forms.caution: Placed too late it loses readers, too early it wastes the lede's momentum — conventionally paragraphs three to six.

journalism_forms.name: anecdotal lede
journalism_forms.definition: Open on a scene or person rather than on the news, deferring the general claim.
journalism_forms.caution: Requires a nut graf within a few paragraphs or the reader cannot tell what they are reading.

journalism_forms.name: five ws lede
journalism_forms.definition: A summary opening that answers who, what, when, where, why and how in a sentence or two.
journalism_forms.caution: Cramming all six produces the unreadable lede; pick the two that are actually news.

journalism_forms.name: tick-tock
journalism_forms.definition: Minute-by-minute reconstruction of how an event unfolded, assembled from multiple sources.
journalism_forms.effect: Tension comes from the reader knowing the outcome and watching the participants not know it.
journalism_forms.register: post-crisis reporting, disaster and deal narratives

journalism_forms.name: explainer
journalism_forms.definition: Arrangement built on the questions a non-expert would ask, in the order they would ask them.
journalism_forms.caution: Question order is the whole craft; expert-ordered explainers answer question four first.

journalism_forms.name: q and a format
journalism_forms.definition: Edited interview presented as questions and answers, with the arrangement carried by question sequence.
journalism_forms.effect: Preserves the subject's voice and shifts responsibility for claims onto them, which cuts both ways.

journalism_forms.name: profile structure
journalism_forms.definition: A person rendered through scene, biography and the testimony of others, organized around a governing tension.
journalism_forms.caution: Without a tension it becomes a résumé with adjectives; the subject's self-description is not the tension.

journalism_forms.name: obituary structure
journalism_forms.definition: Death, significance, life in brief, defining achievement, personal detail, survivors.
journalism_forms.register: news obituary; the arrangement is fixed enough that departures read as editorial comment

journalism_forms.name: review structure
journalism_forms.definition: Describe the work, place it in context, evaluate against a stated standard, and recommend.
journalism_forms.caution: The standard must be visible; unstated criteria make a review a report of the reviewer's mood.

journalism_forms.name: listicle
journalism_forms.definition: Enumerated arrangement where each item is self-contained and the order carries the argument.
journalism_forms.effect: Sets the reader's expectation of length and effort, which is why it converts; the cost is that the connective argument disappears.

journalism_forms.name: to-be-sure paragraph
journalism_forms.definition: A paragraph acknowledging the strongest objection or the limits of the argument, conventionally placed before the close.
journalism_forms.caution: Ritualized into meaninglessness in opinion writing; a to-be-sure that concedes nothing signals the writer knows the weakness and is stepping around it.

journalism_forms.name: kicker
journalism_forms.definition: A final line or paragraph chosen for resonance rather than information.
journalism_forms.effect: The last thing read and the most quoted; earn it with an image or line already planted earlier.

journalism_forms.name: live blog
journalism_forms.definition: Reverse-chronological accretion in which the arrangement is imposed by time and later revised by summary.
journalism_forms.caution: Readers arrive at the top and read backwards; every entry must carry its own context.

essay_forms.name: five-paragraph theme
essay_forms.definition: Introduction with a three-part thesis, three body paragraphs, and a restating conclusion.

beats.name: introduction
beats.purpose: Funnel to a thesis naming three supports.

beats.name: first support
beats.purpose: Topic sentence, evidence, analysis.

beats.name: second support
beats.purpose: Topic sentence, evidence, analysis.

beats.name: third support
beats.purpose: Topic sentence, evidence, analysis.

beats.name: conclusion
beats.purpose: Restate and generalize.

essay_forms.caution: A scaffold for learners, not a form; its symmetry forces three reasons whether or not three exist.

essay_forms.name: delayed-thesis essay
essay_forms.definition: The claim is withheld until the evidence has been walked, so the reader reaches it as a conclusion.

beats.name: occasion
beats.purpose: Open on the problem, scene or anomaly, not the claim.

beats.name: exploration
beats.purpose: Work through evidence and competing readings.

beats.name: narrowing
beats.purpose: Eliminate the alternatives that fail.

beats.name: thesis
beats.purpose: State the claim the reader has been assembling.

essay_forms.register: op-eds for hostile audiences, literary essays

essay_forms.name: braided essay
essay_forms.definition: Two or more distinct strands alternated in sections, related by resonance rather than by argument.

beats.name: strand a
beats.purpose: Establish the first line — often personal or narrative.

beats.name: strand b
beats.purpose: Introduce the second — often researched or historical.

beats.name: alternation
beats.purpose: Cut between strands so each recontextualizes the other.

beats.name: convergence
beats.purpose: Bring the strands into contact without stating the equation.

essay_forms.caution: The reader must be able to feel the connection by the second alternation; explaining it kills the form.

essay_forms.name: segmented essay
essay_forms.definition: Numbered or white-space-separated sections whose gaps carry as much meaning as the text.
essay_forms.caution: The gaps must do work; segmentation used to hide missing transitions is visible immediately.

essay_forms.name: lyric essay
essay_forms.definition: An essay organized by image, rhythm and association rather than by claim and support.
essay_forms.caution: The absence of argument is a choice that must be paid for in precision elsewhere.

essay_forms.name: hermit crab essay
essay_forms.definition: An essay that borrows an unrelated document's form — recipe, syllabus, field guide, court filing — and inhabits it.
essay_forms.effect: The borrowed form supplies constraint and irony at once; the mismatch between shell and content is the argument.
essay_forms.caution: One-joke risk; the form has to keep generating meaning past the recognition.

essay_forms.name: exploratory essay
essay_forms.definition: Arranged as a record of inquiry — the question, the false starts, the revisions — rather than as a report of its conclusion.
essay_forms.caution: Requires genuine uncertainty; staged wandering toward a predetermined answer reads as condescension.

essay_forms.name: cause-and-effect essay
essay_forms.definition: Arranged from causes to consequences, or backwards from an outcome to its causes.
essay_forms.caution: Correlation dressed as sequence is the standard failure; state the mechanism, not just the order.

essay_forms.name: definition essay
essay_forms.definition: Establish what a contested term should mean, usually by distinguishing it from near neighbours and testing it against cases.
essay_forms.effect: Frequently the whole argument in disguise: whoever fixes the definition has usually won the dispute.

essay_forms.name: process analysis
essay_forms.definition: Arranged as the ordered stages of how something is done or how it happens.
essay_forms.caution: Two different forms share the name — how to do it, and how it happens; mixing them confuses the reader's role.

essay_forms.name: classification and division
essay_forms.definition: Sort a subject into categories on a single stated principle, then treat each category.
essay_forms.caution: The principle of division must be constant; a taxonomy that switches criteria mid-list is the commonest structural fault in nonfiction.

essay_forms.name: they say / i say
essay_forms.definition: Enter an existing conversation by summarizing what others claim before advancing one's own view.

beats.name: they say
beats.purpose: Summarize the prevailing view fairly and specifically.

beats.name: i say
beats.purpose: State your response — agree, disagree, or both with a difference.

beats.name: reasons and evidence
beats.purpose: Support the response.

beats.name: so what / who cares
beats.purpose: Say who this matters to and why it is worth the argument.

essay_forms.effect: Makes the motive for the piece explicit, which is what most unmotivated essays lack.

essay_forms.name: op-ed structure
essay_forms.definition: News hook, thesis, three supporting arguments, concession, and a call for a specific change.

beats.name: hook
beats.purpose: Tie to something that happened this week.

beats.name: thesis
beats.purpose: State the argument in one sentence, early.

beats.name: argument
beats.purpose: Two or three supports, evidence per support.

beats.name: to be sure
beats.purpose: Concede the strongest objection honestly.

beats.name: call
beats.purpose: Name who should do what.

essay_forms.register: 700-900 words; the constraint is the form

essay_forms.name: abdce
essay_forms.definition: Action, background, development, climax, ending — a narrative arrangement for essays and features.

beats.name: action
beats.purpose: Open in motion, mid-event.

beats.name: background
beats.purpose: Supply what the reader now needs to understand it.

beats.name: development
beats.purpose: Carry the action forward with rising consequence.

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: The decisive moment or realization.

beats.name: ending
beats.purpose: Land on the changed state, briefly.

essay_forms.name: zuihitsu
essay_forms.definition: The Japanese 'follow the brush' form: loosely linked fragments, lists and observations arranged by association.
essay_forms.register: literary nonfiction; the ancestor of the segmented essay by a different route

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: three-point sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: One text, one theme, three parallel points, and an application.

beats.name: introduction
beats.purpose: Establish the need the text addresses.

beats.name: first point
beats.purpose: State, explain, illustrate, apply.

beats.name: second point
beats.purpose: State, explain, illustrate, apply.

beats.name: third point
beats.purpose: State, explain, illustrate, apply.

beats.name: application
beats.purpose: Ask the hearer for a specific response.

speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: The parallelism can force a third point the text does not contain.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: expository sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Arrangement follows the structure of the text itself, verse by verse or unit by unit.
speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: Constrains the preacher's agenda by making the text set the order.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: topical sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Arrangement follows a subject, gathering texts to it.
speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: Places the whole weight on the preacher's selection, which is why it is the easiest form to abuse.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: textual sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: The divisions of a single short passage supply the divisions of the sermon.
speech_and_sermon_forms.register: between expository and topical; useful for a dense verse or two

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: lowry loop
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: A narrative homiletic in five stages that treats the sermon as a plot rather than as an outline.

beats.name: upsetting the equilibrium
beats.purpose: Introduce a discrepancy the hearer feels.

beats.name: analyzing the discrepancy
beats.purpose: Deepen the problem rather than rushing to relieve it.

beats.name: disclosing the clue to resolution
beats.purpose: Turn the problem with an unexpected key, usually from the text.

beats.name: experiencing the gospel
beats.purpose: Let the resolution land as experience, not statement.

beats.name: anticipating the consequences
beats.purpose: Show what living from that resolution looks like.

speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: The most transferable sermon form for secular argument: it is an arc, not a list.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: four pages of the sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Trouble in the text, trouble in the world, grace in the text, grace in the world.

beats.name: trouble in the text
beats.purpose: Name the difficulty inside the passage.

beats.name: trouble in the world
beats.purpose: Locate the same difficulty in the hearers' lives.

beats.name: grace in the text
beats.purpose: Show what the passage does about it.

beats.name: grace in the world
beats.purpose: Show what that means now, concretely.

speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: The two-by-two grid generalizes to any argument that must move between analysis and lived stakes.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: puritan plain-style sermon
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Text, doctrine, reasons, uses — exposition followed by proof followed by application.

beats.name: text
beats.purpose: Read and open the passage in its context.

beats.name: doctrine
beats.purpose: State the general truth the text yields.

beats.name: reasons
beats.purpose: Prove the doctrine from scripture and reason.

beats.name: uses
beats.purpose: Apply it — for instruction, reproof, comfort, examination.

speech_and_sermon_forms.register: seventeenth-century English and colonial preaching; a strikingly clean argument template

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: homily
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: A short exposition tied to the day's reading, aiming at one point rather than a structure.
speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: Brevity is the form; a homily with three points is a short sermon that ran out of time.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: celebration close
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: A closing movement that restates the sermon's good news in rising, patterned language until the congregation participates.
speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: The content of the celebration must be the content of the sermon; otherwise the emotion has no referent.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: call-and-response structure
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Arrangement built around scheduled audience reply, so the speech is composed in units that invite completion.
speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: Changes the unit of composition from paragraph to exchange.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: altar call
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: A closing arrangement that converts assent into an immediate, public, physical act.
speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: The secular analogue — sign here, now, in the room — carries the same ethical burden about pressure and consent.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: eulogy
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Praise of the dead arranged around a governing quality, illustrated by story, and turned toward the living.

beats.name: acknowledgement
beats.purpose: Name the loss and the room's shared grief.

beats.name: the governing quality
beats.purpose: Say what this person was, in one claim.

beats.name: stories
beats.purpose: Two or three specific memories that prove it.

beats.name: turn to the living
beats.purpose: Say what the quality asks of those present.

beats.name: farewell
beats.purpose: Close with the direct address the occasion needs.

speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: Specific and small beats grand and general every time.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: ted-style talk
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Personal opening, one counterintuitive idea, evidence in three movements, and a closing implication.

beats.name: personal opening
beats.purpose: Establish why this speaker, in a scene.

beats.name: the idea
beats.purpose: State the counterintuitive claim plainly.

beats.name: evidence
beats.purpose: Three movements: study, story, demonstration.

beats.name: implication
beats.purpose: What changes if the audience accepts it.

speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: The format rewards counterintuition, which selects for claims that are surprising rather than true.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: stump speech
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: A repeatable arrangement of fixed modules — story, indictment, promise, ask — reordered for each audience.
speech_and_sermon_forms.effect: Repetition across venues is a feature: the modules get tested and the surviving ones harden.

speech_and_sermon_forms.name: acceptance speech
speech_and_sermon_forms.definition: Gratitude, acknowledgement of others, a claim about what the honour represents, and a brief dedication.
speech_and_sermon_forms.caution: The list of thanks is the part the audience tolerates, not the part they came for; the claim is the speech.
